extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, containing 8 languages and released freely for speech recognition and text-to-speech research.
extraction.license: Public domain source data; MLS is released freely to everyone (specific dataset license not stated)
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.citeAs: Pratap, V., Xu, Q., Sriram, A., Synnaeve, G., & Collobert, R. (2020). MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was prepared by downloading LibriVox audiobooks for selected languages, downsampling audio from 48kHz to 16kHz, segmenting long audio into 10-20 second utterances, generating pseudo-labels with acoustic models and a 4-gram language model, retrieving transcripts by matching pseudo-labels to source book text using TF-IDF and Smith-Waterman alignment, and manually extracting text sources when automatic parsing was difficult.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audiobook text source links were invalid or redirected incorrectly; some books had corrupted metadata such as missing title or speaker/author information; some audio contained multiple speakers and was removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobook audio and corresponding book texts, with many texts originating from Project Gutenberg and other domains such as archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, spiegel.de, projekt-gutenberg.de, and zeno.org.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Long audio was segmented into 10-20 second chunks based on silence intervals. Text was normalized with NFKC normalization, removal of punctuation/subscripts/superscripts/emojis/escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphenation, and filtering to valid Unicode characters for the language. Numbers in matched text were replaced using aligned words from pseudo-labels; heuristics were applied for hyphens and apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Books with corrupted metadata were removed; audios with multiple speakers were removed; only latest versions of books with same author/title were kept; candidate transcripts with WER > 40% versus pseudo-labels were filtered out; books overlapping with dev/test by title edit distance or 5-gram overlap were removed; development/test sets were human-verified by correcting clear and obvious transcript errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human transcribers listened to audio while viewing transcripts for the development and test sets and corrected clear and obvious errors. The dataset also includes pseudo-label generation from acoustic models and transcript retrieval via alignment, but human annotation was used for verification of dev/test transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Generated transcripts were compared against human-rated transcripts using WER; examples of corrections include diacritic correction, missing words, and missing apostrophes. The paper reports WER between generated transcript and human rated transcript for dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere, LibriLight, TDS Convolutions with ASG loss, beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model, TF-IDF similarity on bigrams, Smith-Waterman alignment, KenLM, wav2letter++
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender of speakers was inferred for dataset splitting; speakers are balanced in gender in development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote open research in large-scale ASR and multilingual ASR, and can also support TTS research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is based on read audiobooks from LibriVox and Project Gutenberg, which may bias it toward read speech and public-domain book content; development and test sets were balanced in gender and duration.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Training data is lower than the available audiobook data because some text sources were not downloaded, some candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval, and some were filtered when creating valid/test splits. The dataset is limited to 8 languages and read-speech audiobook style. Polish has a high OOV rate that negatively impacts LM decoding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, testing, validation, limited-supervision training benchmarks, ASR research, multilingual ASR, and text-to-speech research.
